claim.quote: We have conducted for the first time a directional dark matter search in an unshielded location, at the sea level, by keeping an emulsion detector exposed for 39 days on an equatorial telescope mount.

key_value.note: Cross sections above this are excluded for a 10 GeV/c^2 dark matter mass; the abstract gives 1.7e-31 cm^2 for 100 GeV/c^2. Confidence level not stated in the abstract.

key_value_text.quote: cross-sections higher than $1.3 \times 10^{-28}$ cm$^{2}$ and $1.7 \times 10^{-31}$ cm$^2$ were excluded for a dark matter mass of $10$ GeV$/c^2$ and $100$ GeV$/c^2$, respectively
key_value_text.value: cross-sections higher than $1.3 \times 10^{-28}$ cm$^{2}$ and $1.7 \times 10^{-31}$ cm$^2$ were excluded for a dark matter mass of $10$ GeV$/c^2$ and $100$ GeV$/c^2$, respectively

name: First direction sensitive search for dark matter with a nuclear emulsion detector at a surface site
notes: Surface exposure at Nagoya University, not at LNGS: no facility recorded on this result.

summary.plain: NEWSdm kept a nuclear emulsion on a telescope mount for 39 days at sea level and saw no deviation from the background, setting a first exclusion plot for this technique.
summary.technical: Emulsion exposure equivalent to 0.59 g d, unshielded, at sea level (Nagoya); angular distribution agrees with the background model; exclusion in the mass-cross-section plane; the first direction-sensitive search with a solid-state tracking detector.

title: First direction sensitive search for dark matter with a nuclear emulsion detector at a surface site
why_it_matters: The abstract says it is the first direction-sensitive search for dark matter with a solid-state, particle tracking detector.
